items.note: Both are seccomp syscall-filter confinement; PWN frames it as an exploitation constraint, JAL as a sandbox boundary. Same mechanism, two domains.
Identical solver behaviour: extract constraints, discharge with Z3/angr. COD frames it as a puzzle, REV as a flag check.
Both require scripting a client to satisfy a networked protocol faster than a human.
Container escape appears as the whole challenge in JAL and as one link of the chain in FPN.

Same concealment move - the logic is not in the DEX - with a different substrate: a native library in MOB-002, an engine bytecode asset in MOB-009. The recovery differs accordingly (reverse the .so vs decompile the bundle).

Both deliver a compiled artifact instead of source. REV-007 stays within one language (its own decompiler); MOB-009 adds the container question - where the bundle hides in the package - and an engine/version triage before any decompiler applies.
